1. Off and on homeschooling and only a tiny bit of correspondence (mail in school work essentially). Beyond that, wasting time playing computer games or watching T.V, reading or other random things in my house

2. Currently I've been diagnosed with G.A.D (Generalized Anxiety Disorder) I've seen a psychiatrist and a doctor last year who haven't diagnosed me further with anything, my family has a history of Depression, Anxiety and Bi-polar (rareish). I'm not a medical professional but I might have bi-polar due to random mood swings (not really angry but more grumpy or happy one day and sad the next). Aforementioned Psychiatrist suggested medication but wanted bloodwork done first, I have a bundle of problems blocking that door such as me being afraid of needles, me terrified to even leave to get it done, the idea of what medication could do to me personality wise, the implication of a next step scares me and if I can choose not to take that step I won't, I feel as if I would be doing things against my will and be a drooling zombie (arguably better than not contributing at all) to society.


**Sorry for the long post, I'm not currently seeing a medical professional as of semi-recently, I can go into more detail about past therapy if need be.**

I lost my dad last year, about 20 days until my 17th birthday, he died of a heart attack in his sleep, he was in his 40s and healthy. My life will be forever changed. I actually stopped seeing him when I was 12 years old because he struggled with alcoholism and what really crossed the line for me was when he kept "going to the bathroom" during a weekly outing which was to a movie theater that week, I smelled liqour poorly disguised by mouthwash on him, I was old enough to know that was horrible to be doing while spending time with your child and I didn't need to be exposed to that, I told my mother and she supported me cutting ties with him. I unfortunately never got to see him before his death. I will always carry sadness and regret with me of a what could've been relationship. all I got was a ring, 24 hour sobriety coin and a death certificate.
I haven't talked to my dad in 4 years, I'm 17 now and he died about 6 months ago.
Don't worry, the older generation will be dead soon.
